headline: Scorpio Gold drills 36-metre gold intercept at Goldwedge
dek: The Nevada driller's Phase Two program also returned high-grade hits at West Pit, Black Mammoth and the Zanzibar Trend, with a sonic program to follow.
caption: Drill rigs worked through the night at a remote Nevada gold project this autumn, part of an ongoing exploration campaign.

sources.title: Scorpio Gold Drills 2.94 g/t Gold over 36.42 Metres from 169.62 Metres at the Goldwedge Target at Manhattan

unverified_claims: The quality-control verification process described (laboratory certificates, field logs, blank/standard/duplicate sample review, chain-of-custody) is as stated by the company and has not been independently audited by this publication.
The inferred resource estimate of 740,000 ounces of gold at Manhattan is drawn from the company's own technical report dated October 23, 2025 (effective June 4, 2025).
The sonic drilling program and the evaluation of underground mining potential at Goldwedge are the company's own stated plans.
brief: Scorpio Gold Corp. (NASDAQ: SGLD) (TSXV: SGLD) reported assay results from eight holes of its Phase Two drill program at the Manhattan District in Nevada. The lead intercept, hole 26MN-124 at the Goldwedge target, returned 2.94 g/t gold over 36.42 metres from 169.62 metres, including 19.33 g/t gold over 4.27 metres from 188.36 metres.

Other holes also returned gold: 24.85 g/t over 1.22 metres at West Pit, 1.37 g/t over 17.07 metres at Black Mammoth (including a higher-grade 17.04 g/t over 1.07 metres), and 1.18 g/t over 17.10 metres along the Zanzibar Trend. The company said the results lie within faulted Zanzibar and Gold Hill formation rock.

The company said it has scheduled a sonic drilling program, due to begin before the end of October, to test the grade and tonnage of Manhattan's historic heap leach pad, tailings pond and low-grade stockpile. Manhattan carries a maiden inferred resource of 740,000 ounces of gold.
body: Scorpio Gold Corp. (NASDAQ: SGLD) (TSXV: SGLD) (OTCQB: SRCRF) (FSE: RY9) on October 14, 2026 reported assay results from eight holes drilled as part of the Phase Two program at its wholly owned Manhattan District project in the Walker Lane Trend of Nevada. The lead result, hole 26MN-124 at the Goldwedge target, returned 2.94 g/t gold over 36.42 metres from a depth of 169.62 metres, including a higher-grade interval of 19.33 g/t gold over 4.27 metres from 188.36 metres, within faulted Zanzibar and Gold Hill formation rock.

Hole 26MN-125 at West Pit returned 24.85 g/t gold over 1.22 metres from 150.88 metres within the Gold Hill Formation. Hole 26MN-121 at Black Mammoth returned 1.37 g/t gold over 17.07 metres from 275.54 metres within Zanzibar Formation mudstone, including a higher-grade 17.04 g/t gold over 1.07 metres at the brecciated contact between the Zanzibar mudstone and limestone units. Hole 26MN-122, along the Zanzibar Trend, returned 1.18 g/t gold over 17.10 metres from 47.21 metres, including 5.58 g/t gold over 2.59 metres, within brecciated metasediments of the Gold Hill Formation.

The company said the results were verified by Leo Hathaway, P.Geo., its executive technical director, through review of laboratory certificates and field logs, inspection of blank, standard and duplicate sample performance, and chain-of-custody records. The release said assays have now been reported for 115 of the 122 holes drilled in the Phase Two program, totalling 33,379 of 35,844 metres, with results pending on the remaining seven holes.

Manhattan carries a maiden inferred mineral resource estimate of 740,000 ounces of gold, from 18,343,000 tonnes grading 1.26 g/t gold, with an effective date of June 4, 2025 and a technical report dated October 23, 2025. The project includes the Goldwedge mine and four past-producing pits across a 4,780-hectare property in which Scorpio Gold holds a 100% interest.

The company said it has scheduled a sonic drilling program, due to begin before the end of October 2026, to provide an initial test of the grade and tonnage of Manhattan's historic heap leach pad, tailings pond and low-grade stockpile. It also said it continues to evaluate underground mining potential at Goldwedge.
